v4.9.076 - a sync stops closing what you have open (#352, #353)

#352 The pull's branch that protects frames holding unsent work - which is, by
     definition, the frame you just photographed - reset the card to its FIRST
     version and skipped the code that restores what each card was showing. So
     the photo appeared, the push went, the pull came back, and the card fell to
     the main frame. Every time on a photo; only sometimes elsewhere, because an
     empty pull no longer rebuilds anything (#349). Also stopped the pull
     switching the shooting-order view off.

#353 The same rebuild also turned SETUPS off, cleared which setup was selected,
     and dropped the group you were filtered to. Open SETUPS, tag a frame, and
     the sync that followed closed it. Those three are what the person decided a
     second ago; a sync has nothing to say about them. The group is still
     dropped if it no longer exists after the merge.

The rule that chooses 3x2 when a project OPENS is untouched.

#354 And it does not put your pen down. drawActive - "this card is in drawing
     mode right now" - was cleared on every pull, so finishing a stroke ended
     the drawing: the stroke pushes, the pull comes back, and the card drops out
     of draw mode into the plain grid. Pen width and eraser go with it.

#355 The rest of the same list, swept in one pass rather than one at a time:
     reorder mode is no longer cancelled by a sync, the clipboard is no longer
     emptied, and WHICH shooting order you are looking at is yours rather than
     something that travels in the project's metadata from the other device.

The whole family is one mistake: the pull rebuilt the SCREEN along with the
PROJECT. A sync brings work from elsewhere. What is in front of you - the view,
the open panel, the selected setup, the pen, the card you expanded, the order
you are reading - was decided by the person holding the device a second ago.
